question: What crash modification factor for installing an ALL-WAY plaque is listed in Table 2B-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence does not support this question. Table 2B-1 in the MUTCD is a table of Regulatory Sign and Plaque Sizes (giving sign dimensions for conventional roads, expressways, freeways, minimum, and oversized applications) — it does not list crash modification factors, and none of the provided evidence contains any crash modification factor for the ALL-WAY (R1-3P) plaque. The MUTCD does not publish crash modification factors; those are found in other resources (e.g., the CMF Clearinghouse or the Highway Safety Manual), not in this manual. Standards (mandatory): - For context only, the ALL-WAY plaque requirement is: "At intersections where all approaches are controlled by STOP signs (see Section 2B.12), an ALL-WAY (R1-3P) supplemental plaque (see Figure 2B-1) shall be mounted below each STOP sign. The ALL-WAY plaque shall have a white legend and border on a red background." No crash modification factor is stated. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Figure 2B-1 with the R1-3P ALL WAY plaque and related STOP/YIELD plaques, but contains no crash modification factor; the Table 2B-1 page visible in the attached full-page material lists only sign and plaque sizes (e.g., All Way plaque R1-3P at 18 x 6), not safety effectiveness data. Citations: - Section 2B.04 Standard §4 (p.74) - Figure 2B-1 (p.74)
gold_answer: The MUTCD does not specify this information. A correct response should state that the requested value or requirement cannot be determined from the manual rather than inventing an answer.
